newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis sees strong agribusiness growth.
newsitem.headline: Novartis sees strong agribusiness growth.

text.p: Novartis chief executive Daniel Vasella said he expected its agribusiness to grow nearly 10 percent a year and that its purchase of Merck's crop protection business had completed its acquisition plans in the sector.
"Of course we do not expect double-digit growth in our agribusiness, but growth rates should not be much below 10 percent," he told the Basler Zeitung newspaper in an interview.
"Agribusiness is thus an interesting segment. You also have to see that we can expect a higher return because we are global leaders. Our size gives us economies of scale," he said.
World population growth and rising disposable income will fuel demand for more and better food, he said, estimating demand would grow two to three percent a year over the long term.
"Crop protection is thus a growth business. The same is true for the seeds business, in which we are also strong," he said.
Vasella said the $910 million purchase of Merck's crop protection unit rounded out Novartis's plans for the segment.

"We have pretty much finished our worldwide positioning in crop protection with this deal," he said. "In the future we can presumably concentrate on internal growth. Of course this does not mean that I am ruling out any future takeovers."
